title: Seal the staged desktop runtime and refuse a failed seal
text: Packaging should seal the staged Electron.app before its files are inventoried, so macOS can check the copied runtime. In scripts/package.mjs add and export sealElectronBundle(bundle, execute), where execute defaults to spawnSync and is called as execute(path, args, options). It runs /usr/bin/codesign twice, in this order: first with --force --deep --sign - --preserve-metadata=identifier,entitlements and the bundle path, then with --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 and the bundle path. The options are an environment of LANG=C and PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, utf8 encoding, a 30000 millisecond timeout, a 65536 byte buffer limit and stdio ignore, pipe, pipe. If a step reports an error, a non-zero status or a signal, throw an Error whose message is "The staged Electron resource seal did not finish successfully." and run no later step. When both steps succeed, return { kind: 'ad-hoc', verified: 'deep-strict', developerID: false, notarized: false }. packageDesktop calls it on the staged Electron.app before the inventory and records the result as the signature next to the Electron version in the manifest.

checks.name: package-seal
args: --test-name-pattern=staging refuses a failed or unfinished seal or verification

verification.method: The checks ran in a clean export of the base commit with the hidden files from the solution commit in place, and had to fail. They then ran in a clean export of the solution commit, and had to pass. Installed dependencies were linked from the checkout, and the checks ran with a minimal environment and a temporary home.
